construction.name: complete_prism_source_affine_self_enclosure
construction.proof:
COMMON-AXIS PRISM TRANSFER INTO THE SUPPORTED SELF HOST

The live catalog supports self hosts only at canonical prism height 1.
Consequently simply transferring a height-h self-host row to a new host
height is not a supported-record operation. Instead retain a complete
native source from any current host and apply the already reviewed common
axis map to its owners, then enclose all actual vertices in the supported
height-one prism. This is a new finite enclosure of a complete source,
not an assertion that the old host maps to the desired new host.

For source axes R_i e3=+/-d, source height h, and target height H=1, use
A=I+(1/h-1)dd^T/(d.d). Then A R_i=R_i diag(1,1,1/h), so every complete
source owner becomes exactly one target owner, with the same frame. The
same invertible A applies to all centers and preserves pair disjointness.
When h=1 the identity map is retained as an actual re-enclosure control.
In this identity case no axis hypothesis is needed, so every complete
height-one source is eligible, including its arbitrary inherited frames.

Let a_f.x<=beta_f be every canonical target-host wall. With transformed
centers p_i=A c_i, compute b_f=max_(i,v) a_f.(p_i+R_i v), over ALL target
owner vertices. The common enclosure is the four-variable system
  a_f.t - beta_f*S <= -b_f for every f,
minimizing S with one shared t. This charges every physical host wall and
owner, without choosing an independent scale or translation per wall.
The metric solve only realizes this derived finite enclosure operation.

Before promotion, check source native geometry, actual rational axes and
canonical height identity, and all target native vertices and pair gaps.
One common center dilation and outward host padding handles final rounding.
Retain source path/hash/attribution, A, its inverse, the common translation,
all attaining wall owners/vertices, every unchanged frame, and the inverse
owner map. A failed fixed-source enclosure is not a global obstruction.

construction.name: marked_pentagonal_prism_edge_dimer_return
construction.proof:
MARKED PENTAGON EDGE-DIMER RETURN

Let P be the canonical regular pentagonal prism and choose one actual
vertical side face. Its centroid m=(mx,my,0) is the radial midpoint of the
marked base edge. Put a complete copy of P at -m and its half-turn about
the prism axis at +m. Because the prism is symmetric in z, the second
copy is the central image -P. The marked edge face of the first and the
opposite marked edge face of the second now both lie in the plane
m dot x=0, with their interiors on opposite sides. This is one complete
two-owner module, with a retained common separator and marked source face.

The module is centrally symmetric and its rectangular bounding box is
computed from ALL vertices of BOTH owners. Treat that box as a whole cell
in the complete grid/row/layer constructions. The two owners and their
shared face are never independently repositioned. Deletion, if used for
an odd final count, removes a named whole owner and preserves its complete
parent module and cell.

The five actual side faces give five marked host registrations of this
same source operation. They form a finite exact list, not an angle sweep.
The source is classical edge gluing; no new infinite pentagon packing is
claimed. Every resulting finite witness must improve a pinned baseline
and pass native and independent complete geometry/decoder checks.
construction.native_decoder: Compute the exact centroid m of the marked canonical side face. In each centered module-grid cell place the canonical owner at -m and the z-half-turn owner at +m. Retain the listed whole-owner words; multiply every resulting center by1.0000001 and use nominal_s*1.0000001+1e-7, rounded upward.

contribution.method:
This is an explicit replacement archive for 23 previously submitted cases, adding zero new distinct campaign cases. SUPERSESSIONS.json identifies the prior issue, archive, native hash and certified scale for each case. Ten replacements improve the pinned current nominal/reference bound; thirteen improve the complete native certificate without claiming a new ideal nominal value.

These complete constructions combine forced-phase prism-to-antiprism ring/slot inclusion, literal whole-owner prefixes, prism column and height/collar transfers, and retained whole-row returns. Every source has a full physical decoder with actual owner centers and frames. Certificate improvements arise from these physical operations; their narrower numerical scope is retained explicitly.

All active witnesses passed independent source, full geometry and current-public/private comparison review, followed by both official checks on the packaged native files. The archive preserves the complete source chain, original donor attribution, reviewed intermediate packings and explicit supersession identities. Some provenance audit scripts require the authenticated upstream Git snapshot or reviewed-source registry; the bundled official native validators are directly replayable.

Credit the new finite constructions exactly to PingYou Ltd. Original donors and their authors remain credited. These contributions may be published under the repository’s MIT license. No global optimum is claimed. Please treat these as stronger replacements, not as 23 additional distinct cases.
